ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the graphs of the functions $y_1=kx$ and $y_2=ax+3$ intersect at point $A(-1, 2)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $kx>ax+3$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} By observing the graph, we can see that when $x<-1$, the line $y_1=kx$ is above the line $y_2=ax+3$. \\
Therefore, the solution set for the inequality $kx>ax+3$ with respect to $x$ is $x<-1$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{x<-1}$.
